bounds: Startup investing means putting money into a young private company in exchange for a security, such as shares or an agreement that may convert into shares later.
You are not buying a guaranteed piece of a future success story.
The company may grow, stay small, change direction, or close, and your investment can lose all its value.
Unlike a public stock, a private startup investment usually has no active market where you can sell whenever you want.
Before deciding, identify exactly what security is offered, what rights it gives, how the business plans to use the money, and what could go wrong.
Think of the money as money you may not see again for a long time.
A compelling founder or product is only one part of the decision.
Read the actual offering documents, compare the price and terms, and decide whether the risk fits your finances.
Education is not a recommendation to invest, and no platform can promise a startup’s outcome.
